narrativeReportMd:
# Contributor R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Contributor` is a hard breaking removal from the R6 core datatype set. R4 content that uses a `Contributor` datatype, especially polymorphic JSON names such as `valueContributor`, has no same-named R6 StructureDefinition and will not validate or deserialize as an R6 core type.

## Scope
The analysis compared the R4 `Contributor` StructureDefinition to the R6 core package. The assigned R6 StructureDefinition file is absent, the R6 package index contains no `Contributor` StructureDefinition, and exact searches found no `StructureDefinition/Contributor`, `"Contributor"` type, or `contributor-type` terminology artifact. Inherited `Element`/`DataType` hierarchy changes and detailed changes in consumer resources are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
This is mostly a removal and conversion problem rather than a field-by-field evolution. R4 `Contributor` bundled a required role code (`author`, `editor`, `reviewer`, `endorser`), a required contributor name, and optional `ContactDetail` contacts. R6 keeps `ContactDetail` and has many contextual metadata elements named `author`, `editor`, `reviewer`, and `endorser`, but the role is then expressed by the containing element path rather than by a `Contributor.type` field. Generic R4 `Contributor` values therefore need context-specific mapping or an extension/profile strategy.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is the missing R6 datatype identity. The next practical issue is that the role/name/contact bundle has no one-to-one R6 replacement, especially for systems that stored generic Contributor values outside a specific author/editor/reviewer/endorser element. A related runtime/codegen risk is removal from broad choice elements such as `Parameters.parameter.value[x]`, `Task.input.value[x]`, and `ElementDefinition.defaultValue[x]`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for deciding the target model when a Contributor value is not already tied to a parent author/editor/reviewer/endorser element. The local package confirms absence but does not include the official design rationale or a cross-version ConceptMap.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Because `Contributor` was draft/trial-use and appears rarely as a direct element type in R4 core, removal may be justified. A less disruptive design would have kept a deprecated compatibility datatype or retained it in the generic type universe while recommending role-specific `ContactDetail` elements for new content.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze `ContactDetail`, `MetadataResource`, and specific knowledge-artifact resources/profiles that consumed contributor semantics. Also review base `DataType`/`Element` reports for inherited datatype-superclass effects.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Contributor` is absent from the R6 core package, so R4 data or generated code that depends on this datatype is breaking. The top migration concerns are replacing generic `Contributor` values, preserving the required role/name semantics, and handling removed `valueContributor`-style polymorphic representations. The main uncertainty is the lack of an official replacement map or narrative migration note.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is context-dependent. Where an R4 `Contributor.type` value is known from context, systems can often map `author`, `editor`, `reviewer`, or `endorser` to the corresponding R6 role-specific element carrying `ContactDetail`. Generic `Contributor` values in `Parameters`, `Task`, profiles, StructureDefinitions, or custom extensions need explicit policy: transform to a role-specific field, use a cross-version/custom extension, or preserve the raw R4 fragment outside the R6 core model. The role code and the nested contact details should be tested because a naive `Contributor` to `ContactDetail` transform can lose role or contact grouping information.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the removal conclusion because the R4 StructureDefinition and index contain `Contributor`, while the assigned R6 file is absent, the R6 index has no exact StructureDefinition match, exact package searches found no `Contributor` type or `contributor-type` terminology, and R6 type-system terminology does not include a `Contributor` concept. Confidence is medium for replacement guidance because the local package does not include an official diff, ConceptMap, or narrative explanation of the intended migration path.

facts.note: Low maturity reduces expected prevalence but not the technical breaking effect.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: A same-canonical or same-type match was not found. R6 uses `ContactDetail` in contextual author/editor/reviewer/endorser elements, but that is a modeling pattern rather than a same-identity datatype replacement. The most reliable conclusion from local package evidence is deletion or non-one-to-one replacement.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and type-identity break: an R4 `Contributor` JSON fragment or any R4 instance using a `Contributor` choice value cannot be validated against R6 core because there is no R6 datatype definition or choice type. Runtime impact is high for code generators, validators, serializers, profile processors, and transformation engines that expect every R4 datatype to have an R6 counterpart.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The datatype carries authorship/review/endorsement metadata for knowledge artifacts. Loss or misclassification can affect governance and auditability, but no direct patient-safety calculation was identified from the datatype alone.

justification.inferredGoal: Remove a rarely used trial-use datatype and rely on context-specific ContactDetail-based metadata elements.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `Contributor` as a deprecated R6 datatype and compatibility choice while steering new content to role-specific `ContactDetail` elements.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: remove a draft/trial-use generic role-bearing datatype and rely on contextual `author`, `editor`, `reviewer`, and `endorser` elements of type `ContactDetail`. A less-breaking base design was available in principle, so the break is not uniquely required. However, that design has material long-term costs because R6 implementations would need to keep accepting a parallel `Contributor` model even while the preferred model expresses the role structurally. On the local evidence, the removal is therefore probably justified rather than fully justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base R6 alternative would have kept `StructureDefinition/Contributor` in the core package with deprecated or legacy status, preserved its `type`, `name`, and `contact` shape, and kept it in broad choice domains for compatibility. New R6 definitions could still recommend role-specific `ContactDetail` elements. This is a real base-design alternative, not merely conversion tooling, but it only partially meets the cleanup goal because it perpetuates two ways to represent the same contribution semantics.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves most R4 `Contributor` values, but keeps a low-use trial-use datatype, duplicate contribution representations, and validator/codegen support that R6 appears to be retiring.

examples.examplesMd: The example is a datatype fragment rather than a complete resource. It illustrates the R4 `Contributor` shape; in R6 there is no `Contributor` datatype against which this fragment can validate.

findings.narrativeMd: `Contributor` itself disappeared from the R6 core package. This is broader than an element tweak: R4 systems may have generated a `Contributor` class, accepted `valueContributor` in generic choice fields, or used the canonical URL in profiles. R6 validators and serializers have no local definition to bind those references to.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 value whose declared type is `Contributor` is old-valid/new-invalid in R6 unless it is transformed into some other R6 structure. This affects strict JSON/XML parsers, FHIRPath/type checks, generated model packages, schema validators, and profile processors. R6-to-R4 representability is marked not applicable for this artifact-level finding because R6 has no `Contributor` content to send back as the same type.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all uses of `Contributor`, including `valueContributor`, profile defaults/fixed/pattern/example values, custom extensions, StructureMaps, and generated APIs. For each use, choose a target: a context-specific `author`/`editor`/`reviewer`/`endorser` element of type `ContactDetail`, a cross-version/custom extension preserving the R4 shape, or manual migration outside the R6 core model. Tests should include unknown role contexts and nested contact details.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal could have been made less disruptive by keeping `Contributor` as deprecated in R6 or retaining it in broad choice elements for compatibility. That would preserve old data and codegen shape, but it would also keep a low-use role-bearing datatype if the intended R6 design is to express contribution role through the containing element path.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The local package did not contain an official explanation. If an HL7 ballot diff identifies a formal replacement, this finding's migration guidance should be updated.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 defines `Contributor` as a concrete datatype, but the R6 package has no matching StructureDefinition, package-index entry, or FHIR type code. That is a real top-level type identity break: validators, profile processors, generic choice handling, and generated SDKs that know the R4 datatype cannot resolve the same canonical/type in R6. The datatype is specialized and trial-use, so I would not infer common production prevalence from the break alone, but complete deletion of a named datatype used by broad choice machinery is stronger than ordinary metadata churn.
keyEvidence: R6 package: no StructureDefinition-Contributor.json and no exact .index.json StructureDefinition entry for Contributor.
R4 CodeSystem-data-types contains code Contributor; R6 CodeSystem-fhir-types has no Contributor code.
R4 maturity map reports standardsStatus=trial-use and no numeric FMM for Contributor.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The available maturity signal is trial-use rather than normative/mature. That softens assumptions about broad production reliance, but it does not eliminate concern because the finding is complete datatype identity removal rather than a narrow element cleanup.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: R6 has no datatype definition or type-system code for an R4 Contributor, so generated classes, validators, serializers, and canonical-resolution tooling lose a formerly valid type identity.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base R6 design appears plausible: retain `Contributor` as a deprecated legacy datatype for one release, ideally still available to broad choice elements, while steering role-specific resource metadata toward ContactDetail paths. The tradeoff is carrying an obsolete role-embedded model and extra codegen surface, but that cost seems modest compared with deleting the type outright.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high hard/runtime impact, but the fresh review adds an explicit less-breaking base alternative and tempers prevalence because the R4 signal is trial-use.

findings.title: Contributor's required role/name/contact bundle has no one-to-one R6 replacement

oldState.summary: R4 Contributor carries a required role code plus required contributor name and optional contact details.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R4 CodeSystem explicitly defines the four role codes. No R6 `contributor-type` ValueSet or CodeSystem was found, and no expansion service was used.

oldState.narrativeMd: `Contributor.type` is mandatory in R4 and uses a required binding to distinguish author, editor, reviewer, and endorser. `Contributor.name` is also mandatory, and `Contributor.contact` can carry one or more `ContactDetail` values.

newState.summary: R6 has no Contributor.type element or contributor-type terminology; role is only inferable from context where role-specific elements exist.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 has no `Contributor` datatype, no `Contributor.type` element, and no local `contributor-type` terminology artifact. R6 resources such as `MetadataResource`/knowledge artifacts use contextual elements such as `author`, `editor`, `reviewer`, and `endorser` of type `ContactDetail`, so the role can be represented by the parent path only when the migration target is known.

facts.newValue: No R6 local element; possible contextual ContactDetail.name target is 0..1
No R6 local element; possible contextual ContactDetail.telecom/name target is not a one-to-one structural match

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The best local replacement evidence is not a matched datatype but a modeling pattern: R6 retains `ContactDetail` and uses role-specific parent element names in metadata artifacts. That can preserve some semantics when the original role and target path are known, but it is not a one-to-one datatype mapping.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The validation break is already captured by the artifact-removal finding. This finding captures the semantic and conversion mechanism: the mandatory R4 role code has no local R6 field unless the migration target has a role-specific path. Mapping generic Contributor values to `ContactDetail` alone loses the role; mapping role to parent path is only possible when the surrounding resource model is known. In reverse, an R6 `ContactDetail` in a role path may omit a name, which cannot always populate R4 `Contributor.name` if one tries to reconstruct a Contributor.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The main risk is governance/audit metadata loss or misclassification of authorship, review, or endorsement. This can be business-significant for knowledge artifacts, but no direct clinical safety issue was identified from the datatype alone.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent contribution roles structurally through author/editor/reviewer/endorser elements and reuse ContactDetail for people or organizations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the role-bearing `Contributor` shape for legacy or generic contexts while adding preferred role-specific `ContactDetail` elements for new R6 content.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Representing the contribution role through the containing element path is a coherent R6 design direction, especially where artifacts already expose `author`, `editor`, `reviewer`, and `endorser` paths. The old `Contributor` shape is not just a rename to `ContactDetail`: it carries a mandatory role, a mandatory contributor name, and nested contact details. Keeping it would protect generic R4 values, but would also leave R6 with two structurally different ways to say the same thing and no simple one-to-one rule for all contexts. Those tradeoffs make the breaking design probably justified, though official rationale would be needed for a stronger verdict.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained `Contributor.type` and the rest of the R4 datatype for contexts where no role-specific parent path exists, while making role-specific `ContactDetail` elements the preferred R6 representation. That alternative is only partial because it does not eliminate the old generic role model, can force systems to reconcile both `Contributor` and role-specific `ContactDetail` in the same resource family, and risks deprecated representations remaining indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Improves preservation of R4 role/name/contact bundles, but creates duplicate same-fact representations, ambiguous conversion rules, and ongoing burden for generic containers and profiles.

evidence.detail: R4 `Contributor.type` is required (`1..1`) and bound with required strength to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/contributor-type|4.0.1`.
The R4 contributor-type CodeSystem defines `author`, `editor`, `reviewer`, and `endorser`.

evidence.locator: exact searches for contributor-type and Contributor
evidence.detail: No R6 `contributor-type` ValueSet/CodeSystem or `Contributor` datatype was found in the local package.
R6 metadata elements use `ContactDetail` on role-specific paths, indicating a possible contextual mapping pattern rather than a direct datatype successor.
R6 `ContactDetail.name` is optional (`0..1`), while R4 `Contributor.name` is required (`1..1`).

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is illustrative and assumes a target artifact with a `reviewer` element of type `ContactDetail`. It does not preserve all possible nested `Contributor.contact` structure if multiple contact details have distinct names or telecom groupings.

findings.narrativeMd: The loss of `Contributor` is not just a class-name change. The R4 datatype encoded the contribution role inside the value, while R6's apparent pattern encodes role in the containing element name. Generic stores, Parameters payloads, and custom extensions that held a Contributor without a role-specific parent cannot be transformed by simply renaming the datatype to `ContactDetail`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation fails for raw `Contributor` values because the datatype is absent. Even after choosing a replacement, compatibility can be lossy: `Contributor.type` must become a path or extension, `Contributor.name` may become `ContactDetail.name`, and `Contributor.contact` may need flattening or multiple target contacts. R6-to-R4 reconstruction from a role-specific `ContactDetail` is only reliable if the parent path supplies the role and a usable name is present or can be derived.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not implement a blanket `Contributor -> ContactDetail` transform without considering the role. Use `Contributor.type` to select a target role-specific element when available. Preserve role as an extension when no role-specific target exists. Review multi-contact cases manually or define deterministic rules for copying nested telecom/name data. Test all four role codes and cases with missing, single, and multiple contact details.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The same design goal could have been met less disruptively by keeping `Contributor.type` while adding preferred role-specific elements, or by publishing a formal extension that preserves the removed role field. Those alternatives would improve round-trip behavior but would require R6 implementations to continue carrying a generic contribution role model.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding depends on inferred replacement patterns from local StructureDefinitions. Official ballot notes could confirm or change the intended mapping.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Contributor.type` was required in R4 and carried the role (`author`, `editor`, `reviewer`, or `endorser`) inside the datatype. R6 appears to model these roles through context-specific paths such as `MetadataResource.author`, `editor`, `reviewer`, and `endorser` with `ContactDetail`. That works when the source Contributor is already in a known role context, but it is lossy for generic values such as Parameters, Task inputs/outputs, Extension.value[x], or ElementDefinition fixed/pattern values where the role must remain data rather than be inferred from the containing element name.
keyEvidence: R4 Contributor.type is 1..1 and required-bound to ValueSet contributor-type|4.0.1.
R4 CodeSystem-contributor-type codes are author, editor, reviewer, and endorser.
R6 MetadataResource has author/editor/reviewer/endorser elements of type ContactDetail.
R4 Contributor.name is 1..1, while ContactDetail.name is 0..1 in both R4 and R6.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Trial-use status lowers the compatibility burden relative to normative content, and the likely use is specialized knowledge-artifact metadata. The concern remains meaningful because the removed field is central to the datatype and conversion can require contextual or human judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: mapping Contributor to role-specific ContactDetail paths can preserve the role only when the surrounding R6 path is known; generic or standalone Contributor values have no direct R6 field for the required role code.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Retaining a deprecated `Contributor.type` through a legacy Contributor datatype would preserve generic values. Adding a role field to ContactDetail would be less attractive because ContactDetail is broader than contributor roles and could conflict with R6 role-specific paths. The legacy datatype alternative is still a plausible, more compatible base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing medium conversion-risk assessment, but the fresh review treats the contextual role mapping as a specific lossy-migration reason to revisit rather than merely a rare semantic inconvenience.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The checked R4 broad choice lists explicitly contain `Contributor`; equivalent R6 broad choice lists checked in local StructureDefinitions did not contain it. This is a representation and code-generation consequence of the datatype removal.

impact.impactRationaleMd: FHIR choice elements encode the selected type in the JSON/XML property name. An R4 `Parameters.parameter.valueContributor` or `ElementDefinition.fixedContributor` property will be unknown/invalid in R6 because the type suffix no longer exists. Generated R6 libraries are also unlikely to emit a `Contributor` class, enum member, visitor case, or choice accessor.

justification.inferredGoal: Keep the R6 type universe aligned with the set of actually defined datatypes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Contributor` as a legacy allowed type in broad `value[x]`, fixed, pattern, default, and example choice domains, which requires retaining enough R6 datatype definition to parse it.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Once the base datatype removal is accepted, removing `Contributor` from broad choice type universes is internally consistent and avoids exposing a choice suffix for a type R6 no longer defines. The less-breaking alternative is not a conversion script or extension workaround; it would require retaining `Contributor` as a deprecated base type in the R6 model. That would materially weaken the type-universe cleanup and add codegen and validation burden, so this consequence is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base-design alternative would preserve legacy `Contributor` choice suffixes such as `valueContributor`, `fixedContributor`, `patternContributor`, and `defaultValueContributor` by keeping `Contributor` in the R6 core type list and broad choice definitions. This would protect generic containers and profile metadata during R4-to-R6 migration, but only by continuing to generate and validate a datatype that the rest of R6 is trying to replace with role-specific `ContactDetail` patterns.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves `valueContributor`-style wire compatibility, but forces R6 schemas, validators, generated models, and choice accessors to support a removed datatype indefinitely.

examples.examplesMd: The `Parameters` example illustrates the serialization mechanism. The migration example is not a normative transform; it shows that a system must choose a new parameter contract or encode the data in parts/extensions because `valueContributor` is not available in R6.

findings.narrativeMd: The removal propagates into wire format and generated APIs. FHIR choice names are type-sensitive, so even generic containers that otherwise survived version changes can break on the property name `valueContributor`. This also affects validators and code generators that enumerate all FHIR datatypes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 `Parameters` instance with `valueContributor` can be valid in R4 but invalid in R6. R6 parsers may reject the unknown choice suffix, ignore it as an unknown element depending on leniency, or fail codegen binding because no R6 `Contributor` class exists. The reverse direction has only informational risk because R6 does not generate a `Contributor` suffix.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Search payloads, profiles, StructureDefinitions, StructureMaps, and tests for `Contributor`, `valueContributor`, `fixedContributor`, `patternContributor`, `defaultValueContributor`, and `example.valueContributor`. Replace each occurrence with a version-specific parameter contract, a role-specific `ContactDetail` representation, or an extension that explicitly preserves the old R4 Contributor JSON. Include strict-parser tests so unknown choice suffixes do not disappear silently.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping legacy choice suffixes would have preserved transport compatibility for generic containers, but only if R6 also retained enough datatype definition to parse and validate them. If the design goal was to remove Contributor entirely, the type-domain removal is consistent but necessarily breaking.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is a concrete choice-element wire-format break. In R4, broad choice elements could legally serialize a Contributor as properties such as `valueContributor`, `fixedContributor`, `patternContributor`, or default/example Contributor values. R6 removes Contributor from the checked broad choice lists, so those old-valid properties become unknown or invalid and generated R6 APIs will not expose the corresponding choice arm. The practical prevalence may be low, but the mechanism is direct and not just theoretical.

freshReview.fmmEffect: Trial-use status and specialized use reduce expected prevalence, so I would not score this as broadly disruptive by default. Still, FMM/status does not make an old-valid/new-invalid choice suffix harmless when the base datatype disappears.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 JSON/XML choice property using the Contributor suffix is valid against R4 broad choice definitions but has no corresponding R6 type choice or generated accessor.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept Contributor in the FHIR type set and broad choice lists as deprecated legacy support while encouraging new models to use ContactDetail or role-specific paths. The tradeoff is additional validator/codegen surface for a rarely used type, but it would preserve existing serialized data without difficult precedence rules.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing hard instance and high runtime/codegen concern, while disagreeing with any implication that there is no less-breaking base option; a deprecated legacy choice arm looks feasible.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: R4 `Contributor` has no `Reference`-typed local elements, so there are no local reference-target changes to report.

The only constraints visible on R4 `Contributor` local/inherited elements are generic `ele-1` and extension-related constraints inherited from base artifacts. No Contributor-specific invariant was found.
No R4 `Contributor` local element had a fixed value, pattern, or default value.
No local R4 `Contributor` element had `maxLength`, min/max value, or regex-style limits beyond the primitive datatype definitions handled elsewhere.
R4 `Contributor.type`, `Contributor.name`, and `Contributor.contact` are not modifier elements. The artifact removal does not hide a local modifier-flag change.
No local slicing was present on `Contributor.type`, `Contributor.name`, or `Contributor.contact`. Extension slicing is inherited from `Element`/`Extension` and is out of scope.

The local R4 cardinalities were checked: `type` and `name` are `1..1`, `contact` is `0..*`. Because R6 has no matched `Contributor` element tree, these are treated as removal/conversion effects rather than isolated min/max cardinality changes on retained elements.

R4 marks `Contributor.type`, `Contributor.name`, and `Contributor.contact` as summary elements. Since the R6 artifact is absent, there is no retained local element with a changed summary flag; summary-data loss is part of the artifact removal.

R4 local short/definition text was inspected. There is no R6 `Contributor` narrative to compare; semantic replacement guidance is inferred from related `ContactDetail` and metadata elements and is covered in the findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: ContactDetail remains available as a partial migration target
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `ContactDetail` itself is still present in R6 and retains the same basic `name`/`telecom` shape, so this is not a breaking change in Contributor by itself. It is only a partial target because it does not carry `Contributor.type` and does not exactly model `Contributor.contact` as a list of contact details under a separate contributor name.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Use `ContactDetail` for role-specific R6 fields when the parent path supplies the role. Preserve the R4 role code separately when the target path does not do so.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Direct named R4 core use appears limited outside broad polymorphic containers
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Local searches found `Contributor` primarily as a datatype and in broad choice domains, not as the declared type of common named R4 resource metadata elements such as `Library.author`, which already use `ContactDetail`. This reduces expected prevalence but does not change the hard break for actual Contributor values.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Prioritize generic containers, custom profiles, extensions, and generated datatype APIs when looking for affected systems.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R4 Contributor was draft/trial-use
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 artifact status/maturity helps explain why removal may have been acceptable in the standard, but status does not make existing conformant R4 instances automatically compatible with R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Organizations that adopted draft/trial-use datatypes should expect manual review and should not assume automatic cross-version support.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `ContactDetail` is the likely partial target for preserving contributor names and telecom details, but it is not a complete replacement for `Contributor.type` or nested contact grouping.
R6 contextual author/editor/reviewer/endorser paths on metadata artifacts provide likely migration targets for role-bearing contributor data and should be analyzed in consumer artifact reports.
Any generated-superclass or inherited datatype hierarchy effects belong to the base `DataType`/`Element` reports rather than this local Contributor report.
